newsitem.title: UK: Britain praises Yeltsin for vital summit role.
newsitem.headline: Britain praises Yeltsin for vital summit role.

text.p: Britain on Saturday heaped fulsome praise on a "courageous" Russian President Boris Yeltsin after his summit in Helsinki with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
In a message to Yeltsin, British Prime Minister John Major said: "I welcome the courageous decision that you have made on economic reform and the progress that Russia has achieved."

Major, fighting an election to stay in power, said Yeltsin "has made an increasingly important contribution to recent summits including the special summit on nuclear safety and security he hosted in Moscow last year."
The British leader said it was right that Russia's role as a full participant on global issues be recognised at summits.

At their Helsinki summit on Friday, Clinton and Yeltsin agreed to differ over NATO's expansion plans but vowed to press ahead with a charter defining a new relationship between Moscow and the alliance.
Yeltsin's communist foes in Russia branded the outcome a capitulation.

Clinton brushed aside Russian objections to NATO enlargement into eastern Europe, declaring it would go ahead as planned at a NATO summit in July when Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join.
